text: Chapter six. Gold: is there money without a cave?
Every money in this episode had a Wren. A ship on Yap. Glass from Venice. Iron drills. Shells from Zanzibar. A mint in Rome. Each time, money got easier to make. Usually, the savers paid.
Now gold. All the gold ever mined would fit in one cube, about twenty-three metres on each side. As tall as a seven-storey building. Almost all of it still exists.
cap: Now gold. All the gold ever mined would fit in one cube, about 23 metres on each side. As tall as a seven-storey building. Almost all of it still exists.

text: Each year, the world's mines add a slice on top, less than half a metre thick. Under two percent.
cap: Each year, the world's mines add a slice on top, less than half a metre thick. Under 2%.

text: Gold had its rushes. California in eighteen forty-nine, then Australia. In the eighteen-fifties, the world dug over three times as much gold a year as in the forties. Three times a thin slice is still a thin slice.
cap: Gold had its rushes. California in 1849, then Australia. In the 1850s, the world dug over three times as much gold a year as in the 1840s. Three times a thin slice is still a thin slice.

text: Prices rose. In Britain, where money was gold, by up to a third. They stayed high for about twenty years. Then they fell. By the eighteen-nineties, they were lower than in the forties.
cap: Prices rose. In Britain, where money was gold, by up to a third. They stayed high for about twenty years. Then they fell. By the 1890s, they were lower than in the 1840s.

text: Compare. Cowries: a silver dollar cost ten times more shells. Rome: wheat cost thirty-seven times more. Gold, in the great rushes: prices up to a third higher, for a while. Gold came closest to money without a cave.
cap: Compare. Cowries: a silver dollar cost 10 times more shells. Rome: wheat cost 37 times more. Gold, in the great rushes: prices up to a third higher, for a while. Gold came closest to money without a cave.

text: And today? In ten years, gold's price roughly tripled, with big swings. So digging it pays far more. Still, mine output grew under one percent a year. Nobody has found gold's cave.
cap: And today? In ten years, gold's price roughly tripled, with big swings. So digging it pays far more. Still, mine output grew under 1% a year. Nobody has found gold's cave.
